questions.question: What are fields declared in an interface automatically?
questions.explanation: Interface fields are constants: public static final, whether or not you write those words.

questions.question: Which kind of interface method was added in Java 9?
questions.explanation: Java 8 added default and static methods; Java 9 added private helper methods for them.

questions.question: How many interfaces can one Java class implement?
options: None if it extends a class
questions.explanation: A class extends at most one class but can implement as many interfaces as it needs.

questions.question: What does this print? interface Tune { default String name() { return "tune"; } } class Jingle implements Tune { } ... Tune t = new Jingle(); System.out.println(t.name());
questions.explanation: Jingle does not override name(), so the JVM runs the default body from the interface.

questions.question: interface Skip { void next(); } class Remote implements Skip { void next() { } } Why does Remote fail to compile?
options: next() must be public, since interface methods are public
questions.explanation: Package access is weaker than public, so the implementation must be declared public.

questions.question: interface Volume { int MAX = 100; } ... Volume.MAX = 80; Why does this line fail?
options: MAX is final and cannot be reassigned
questions.explanation: Interface fields are implicitly final constants, so any assignment after declaration is rejected.

questions.question: What does this print? interface Rate { int stars(); } ... Rate r = () -> 4; System.out.println(r.stars() * 2);
questions.explanation: Rate has one abstract method, so the lambda implements it. stars() returns 4, and 4 times 2 is 8.

questions.question: What makes an interface a functional interface?
options: It has exactly one abstract method
questions.explanation: One abstract method is the rule. Default and static methods do not count against it.

questions.question: interface A { default String hi() { return "A"; } } interface B { default String hi() { return "B"; } } class C implements A, B { } Why does C fail to compile?
options: A class cannot implement two interfaces
C inherits two conflicting defaults and must override hi()
questions.explanation: The class must override hi() and may choose one version with A.super.hi() or B.super.hi().

questions.question: How do you call a static method play() declared in interface Player?
questions.explanation: Static interface methods belong to the interface and are called through its name only.
